To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Nesterov acceleration for sampling is possible and it can be achieved via Hessian-Free High Resolution ODEs.

(1) we introduce a Hessian-Free ODE for sampling, and show that it can achieve better sampling efficiency than Langevin, (2) the proposed method can be discretized with a cost of $\mathcal{O}(d)$, (3) it can be implemented with an efficient algorithm, (4) we provide theoretical analysis to support the above claims

1) we prove additional acceleration over under-damped Langevin in W2 distance at continuous-time level; 2) we propose a new algorithm based on Nesterov Accelerated Gradient for Strongly Convex functions; 3) we prove a $\sqrt{d}/ \epsilon$ complexity in W2 distance; 4) we provide a new Hessian-Free High Resolution Discrete Algorithm to efficiently implement the proposed algorithm; 5) we conduct experiments to validate the theoretical results
